key_insight: Fracture toughness in lattice materials is governed by a density-dependent shift from cell-scale failure at low relative density to nodal stress concentration and crack-path geometry at high relative density.
engineering_relevance: The model helps engineers design stronger triangular and hexagonal lattices by tuning relative density, fillet radius, orientation, and base-material ductility to improve damage tolerance.
method: Analytical framework combining homogenization and blunt-crack fracture theory
Finite element simulations across low-to-high relative density regimes
Experimental validation with laser-cut PMMA fracture specimens
evidence_signal: FE results corroborate the model, and experiments in PMMA validate the trends while showing stochastic brittle failure at higher relative densities.
watch_item: Predictions can be sensitive to local crack-tip geometry and stochastic brittle failure, so high-density lattice designs need careful validation before deployment.
paper_title: Fracture of Lattice Materials from Low to High Relative Density
